title.narrative: Awareness raising and capacity building for fight against illicit trafficking of cultural property

description.narrative: Setting fight against illicit import, export and transfer of ownership of cultural property, as one of the priority in the field of culture, Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Serbia, will focus on awareness raising and capacity building of police and customs officers in training with the aim of having them prepared to recognized potential crimes against cultural property and use available tools. The project Awareness raising and capacity building for fight against illicit trafficking of cultural property is a continuation of successfully implemented activities within the project Capacity building for fighting illicit import, export and transfer of ownership of cultural property on local level (Participation Programme 2021-2022). Тhis project included an online workshop and two workshops in the City of Knjaževac ( the Native Museum in Knjaževac) and in the City of Sremska Mitrovica (the City Museum of Srem). The both workshops included a visit to archaeological sites (Timakum Minus archaeological site – Knjaževac and Sirmium Imperial Palace – Sremska Mitrovica) and constructive on-the-spot discussion. The expected results of the project have been entirely fulfilled. Through the implementation of three workshops, all relevant participants in the process of protection of cultural heritage and the fight against illicit trade in cultural property, have undergone a type of training and a comprehensive approach within this process, which includes the readiness of local structures and the establishment of a single procedure concerning activities undertaken in case of illicit import, export and trade, as well as in case of illicit excavation. Workshop participants were introduced to the applicable legislative framework of the Republic of Serbia and the UNESCO conventions concerning this matter, primarily the Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict (The Hague, 1954), the Convention on the Means of Prohibiting and Preventing the Illicit Import, Export and Transfer of Ownership of Cultural Property (Paris, 1970), and Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage (Paris, 1972). The implementation of the project and the participation of all relevant actors at the national and local level contributed to the mapping of new problems in the fight against illicit trade in cultural property and illegal excavations of archaeological sites, but also to establishing previously identified problems on which all departments, each within its competence, work continuously.
